limitations: Definitions fixed before new one-step evaluator calls, after previous development diagnostics. This is exploratory mechanism validation, not fresh confirmation or method selection.

These are new declared native-operator draws, not reconstruction of the consumed original calibration refresh noise. Four draws describe only this finite noise bank, not an exact expected operator or four times as many independent episodes.

Weak target tracking suggests limited width fit/generalization on that bank, not automatically a calibration theorem violation. Tracking its residual while poorly aligning with Q1 optimism supports a proxy-mismatch hypothesis. H/G accounting identifies algebraic differences, not causal proof that changing them improves decisions. G mixes target approximation, lag, smoothing and policy differences.

Training-distribution fitting diagnostic, not held-out calibration, fresh in-distribution validation, or empirical evidence of a conformal coverage guarantee. Multiple rows from one episode are dependent; report unique group count and group-weighted summaries separately.

Saved V is a deterministic numerical continuation conditional on state/action/current actor, with no Monte Carlo return sampling noise. New randomness here is native target-policy smoothing only. Numerical error, population variation and training-seed variation remain separate.
Centered RMS terms can cancel; their magnitudes do not partition error variance or identify causal contributions.
Development candidates are not an in-distribution calibration set. Descriptive containment is not a conformal coverage guarantee.
Constant-vector correlations are undefined and omitted only with explicit counts; states and draws are never inflated into independent action samples.
The math module relies on the caller's source/runtime/replay/transition and frozen-state proof; it performs no model or simulator calls.
